newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kosonic Int'l gets debt reprieve.
newsitem.headline: Kosonic Int'l gets debt reprieve.

text.p: Kosonic International Holdings Ltd said on Friday that it had received written confirmation from its bankers agreeing to a standstill agreement on its debts.
The company said bankers had agreed to withdraw their demands and writs against it and its subsidiaries for a period of 30 days and to be extended to 45 days.

On October 30 the company announced its bankers were considering a standstill agreement and that it was in discussions with potential investors, one of whom was considering providing new loans to Kosonic.
The latest announcement said the company had been approached by a new potential investor who had indicated an interest in subscribing for new shares in the company.
The company has suspended discussions with other, previously indicated, potential investors, the announcement said.

Kosonic also said certain trade creditors had issued writs against it for outstanding debts. However, the notice said Kosonic was in discussions with those creditors with the aim of securing a withdrawal of their claims.

Trading in the shares was suspended on October 23, and since the company is still facing short-term liquidity problems and was unable to pay for raw materials necessary for production, the shares would remain suspended, the announcement said.
